s0301.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Imperial University.
s0301.idiomatic: He was made director of the imperial university.

s0302.literal: Prince Xin'an Bogu once entered the palace and happened upon Yuangui about to lecture; he petitioned to hold the classics, and contemporary opinion deemed it an honor.
s0302.idiomatic: Prince Xin'an Bogu once entered the palace just as Yuangui was about to lecture and petitioned to hold the classics; opinion at the time took it as an honor.

s0303.literal: Soon he was appointed Master of Writing in the Bureau of Temples.
s0303.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed master of writing in the bureau of temples.

s0304.literal: Since Liang times Confucians who transmitted the Zuo tradition had all used Jia Kui and Fu Qian's interpretations to challenge Du Yu—one hundred eighty items in all—Yuangui cited and analyzed them until no doubts remained.
s0304.idiomatic: Since Liang, Zuo-tradition scholars had used Jia Kui and Fu Qian to challenge Du Yu in 180 points; Yuangui cited and analyzed them until nothing was left in doubt.

s0305.literal: Whenever the state deliberated on auspicious and inauspicious great rites, he regularly took part.
s0305.idiomatic: Whenever the state debated great rites of fortune and misfortune, he regularly took part.

s0306.literal: On mother's mourning he left office; when mourning ended, he was made Recorder of the Prince of Poyang's household, soon transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and advanced to Limited Attendant in the Prince of Nanping's household.
s0306.idiomatic: On his mother's death he left office; when mourning ended he became recorder in the prince of Poyang's household, soon regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, then limited attendant in the prince of Nanping's household.

s0307.literal: When the prince went to Jiangzhou, Yuangui followed the prefectural staff; students from all directions came from afar to seek the Way—often several tens or hundreds.
s0307.idiomatic: When the prince went to Jiangzhou, Yuangui followed the staff; students from every quarter came a thousand li to seek instruction—often scores or hundreds at a time.

s0308.literal: In Zhenming year 3 he entered Sui and was made Eastern Pavilion Sacrificial Wine to the Prince of Qin.
s0308.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered Sui and became eastern-pavilion sacrificial wine to the prince of Qin.

s0309.literal: At age seventy-four he died at Guangling.
s0309.idiomatic: At seventy-four he died at Guangling.

s0310.literal: Yuangui authored eleven scrolls of Spring and Autumn Opening Topics and Expository Records, [23] fourteen scrolls continuing Classic Great Meanings, two scrolls of Expository Records on the Classic of Filial Piety, three scrolls of Notes on Zuo's Sounds, and two scrolls of Notes on the Rites' Sounds.
s0310.idiomatic: Yuangui wrote eleven scrolls of Spring and Autumn opening topics and expository records, [23] fourteen scrolls continuing classic great meanings, two on the Classic of Filial Piety, three on Zuo's sounds, and two on the Rites' sounds.

s0311.literal: His son Daye was clever and famed.
s0311.idiomatic: His son Daye was clever and well known.

s0312.literal: At the time Wu commandery's Lu Qing from youth loved study, fully knew the Five Classics, especially excelled in Zuo's Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, and had very high integrity.
s0312.idiomatic: At the time Lu Qing of Wu commandery had loved learning from youth, mastered the Five Classics, and was especially expert in Zuo's Commentary, with very high integrity.

s0313.literal: On first appointment he was Right Ordinary Attendant in the Prince of Wuling's Liang kingdom; he served as Acting Aide in the Ink Bureau of the Campaign-West headquarters and was appointed magistrate of Lou.
s0313.idiomatic: On first appointment he was right ordinary attendant in the prince of Wuling's Liang kingdom, served as acting aide in the campaign-west ink bureau, and was appointed magistrate of Lou.

s0314.literal: When Liang's end brought turmoil, he devoted his mind to Buddhist sutras; no sutra or treatise escaped his study.
s0314.idiomatic: When Liang fell into turmoil he turned his mind to Buddhist sutras and mastered every sutra and treatise.

s0315.literal: Early in Tianchen he was summoned as Undifferentiated Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry but did not accept.
s0315.idiomatic: Early in Tianchen he was summoned as undifferentiated attendant of the scattered cavalry but declined.

s0316.literal: Prince Yongyang as Wu commandery administrator heard his fame and wished to meet him; Qing firmly declined on grounds of illness.
s0316.idiomatic: Prince Yongyang, as Wu commandery administrator, heard of him and wished to meet; Qing firmly pleaded illness.

s0317.literal: His clansman Lu Rong was the commandery's Five Offices aide; Qing once visited him, and the prince went in disguise to Rong's residence and peered through a wall to observe him.
s0317.idiomatic: His clansman Lu Rong was the commandery's five-offices aide; when Qing visited him, the prince went in disguise to Rong's house and watched through a wall.

s0318.literal: The prince told Rong: "Observing Lu Qing's bearing—severe and lofty—he can hardly be fathomed; how could Yan Junping or Zheng Zizhen be set above this?
s0318.idiomatic: The prince told Rong, "Seeing Lu Qing's bearing—severe and lofty—he is hardly fathomable; how could Yan Junping or Zheng Zizhen be ranked above him?

s0319.literal: " The princes of Poyang and Jin'an both summoned him as recorder; he accepted neither.
s0319.idiomatic: " The princes of Poyang and Jin'an both summoned him as recorder; he accepted neither.

s0320.literal: He then built a dwelling in seclusion and took chanting meditation as his business; hence those transmitting the classics and receiving instruction became rare indeed.
s0320.idiomatic: He then built a secluded dwelling and made chanting meditation his occupation; from then on those who transmitted the classics and took pupils were few indeed.

s0322.literal: The historiographer says: To hone the person and exhort conduct, one must first have classical learning; to establish the state and honor the family, all follow this path—thus royal government through it attains perfect order, and human relations through it find their proper sequence.
s0322.idiomatic: The historiographer says: To hone the person and exhort conduct one must first master the classics; to establish the state and honor the family all follow this path—thus royal government through it reaches good order, and human relations through it keep their proper sequence.

s0323.literal: Men like Shen Wena, each specializing in the classics and transmitting instruction, were also great Confucians of a generation.
s0323.idiomatic: Men like Shen Wena, each devoted to the classics and teaching pupils, were great Confucians of their generation as well.

s0324.literal: Wena moreover drafted rites in their first inception—he was nearly of Shusun Tong's kind.
s0324.idiomatic: Wena moreover helped draft rites at their inception—he was nearly in Shusun Tong's class.

s0326.literal: [1] "then the kingly teaching's canon scriptures whereby the former sages illuminate Heaven's Way"—the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions read "the teaching's canon scriptures, then whereby the former sages illuminate Heaven's Way."
s0326.idiomatic: On "then the kingly teaching's canon scriptures whereby the former sages illuminate Heaven's Way": the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions read "the teaching's canon scriptures, then whereby the former sages illuminate Heaven's Way."

s0329.literal: [establish] student slots—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
s0329.idiomatic: On "[establish] student slots": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.

s0330.literal: [3] "overall to instruct with the five classics"
s0330.idiomatic: On "[3] overall to instruct with the five classics"

s0331.idiomatic: Collation variant: (only the National University then classics).

s0332.literal: each classic had its own assistant instructor, etc.—deleted according to the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions.
s0332.idiomatic: On "each classic had its own assistant instructor": deleted per the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions.

s0333.literal: Note: the Southern History preface to the Confucian Scholars biography also lacks these five characters.
s0333.idiomatic: The Southern History preface to the Confucian Scholars biography also lacks these five characters.

s0334.literal: [4] "Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yu Chi received the edict dispatching erudites to deliberate the rites"—"right vice director" in the Southern History reads "left vice director."
s0334.idiomatic: On "[4] right vice director of the masters of writing Yu Chi received the edict dispatching erudites to deliberate the rites": the Southern History reads left vice director for right vice director.

s0335.literal: Note: in Yu Chi's biography, Chi was moved to left vice director in early Tianchen.
s0335.idiomatic: Yu Chi's biography has him moved to left vice director in early Tianchen.

s0336.literal: [5] "ancestor Xiu Zhi"—"Xiu Zhi" in the Southern History reads "Xiu Ji."
s0336.idiomatic: On "[5] ancestor Xiu Zhi": the Southern History reads Xiu Ji for Xiu Zhi.

s0337.literal: The Jinling Bureau edition reads "Xiu Ya"—probably zhi and ya are graphically similar and corrupted.
s0337.idiomatic: The Jinling Bureau edition reads Xiu Ya—probably zhi and ya are shape-similar corruptions.

s0340.literal: [mourning] observers do not remove—changed according to the original text of the Liji "Mourning Garments" minor record.
s0340.idiomatic: On "[mourning] observers do not remove": emended per the original text of Liji, "Mourning Garments," minor record.

s0341.literal: [7] "this is probably the correct point of ritual"—"correct" in the base text was wrong as "host"; other editions are not wrong; now corrected.
s0341.idiomatic: On "[7] this is probably the correct point of ritual": the base text wrongly wrote host for correct; other editions are sound; now emended.

s0342.literal: [8] "body without intact parts"—"zhe" in the Southern and Northern Supervisory and Ji editions all read "fu" (skin).
s0342.idiomatic: On "[8] body without intact parts": zhe in the Southern and Northern Supervisory and Ji editions all read fu (skin).

s0343.literal: Note: the Hanshu biography of Zhang Er and Chen Yu correctly reads "body without intact parts"; writing "fu" for "zhe" is a later unwarranted emendation.
s0343.idiomatic: The Hanshu biography of Zhang Er and Chen Yu correctly reads "body without intact parts"; writing fu for zhe is a later unwarranted change.

s0346.literal: [bring] criminals not to kneel—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions, the Southern History, and Yuan Gui 615.
s0346.idiomatic: On "[bring] criminals not to kneel": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions, the Southern History, and Yuan Gui 615.

s0347.literal: [10] "then [one] on top added four quarter-mark days"—supplied according to the Southern History and Yuan Gui 615.
s0347.idiomatic: On "[10] then [one] on top added four quarter-mark days": supplied per the Southern History and Yuan Gui 615.

s0348.literal: Note: "one on top" means performing graduated punishment once.
s0348.idiomatic: "One on top" means performing graduated punishment once.

s0349.literal: [11] "this was few days"—"correct" in the base text was wrong as "five"; other editions are not wrong; now corrected.
s0349.idiomatic: On "[11] this was few days": the base text wrongly wrote five for correct; other editions are sound; now emended.

s0350.literal: [12] "prisoners have no means to be in the night"
s0350.idiomatic: On "[12] prisoners have no means to be in the night"

s0352.literal: [er] leading to false accusation—changed according to all editions and the Southern History.
s0352.idiomatic: On "[er] leading to false accusation": emended per all editions and the Southern History.

s0353.literal: [13] "while detained he expounded meanings"—the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions read "while detained he explained court-audience meanings"; the Southern History reads "when detained he explained court-audience meanings."
s0353.idiomatic: On "[13] while detained he expounded meanings": the Northern Supervisory and Hall read "while detained he explained court-audience meanings"; the Southern History reads "when detained he explained court-audience meanings."

s0354.literal: [14] "In Taijian repeatedly advanced to [Pacifies] the South Prince of Shixing's staff counsel"—according to the Shixing prince Shuling's biography, in Taijian year 4 he was made General Who Pacifies the South; clearly "south" above lacks "pacifies"; the Southern History has it; now supplied.
s0354.idiomatic: On "[14] in Taijian repeatedly advanced to [pacifies] the south prince of Shixing's staff counsel": Shuling's biography has him made general who pacifies the south in Taijian year 4; south clearly lacks pacifies; the Southern History has it; now supplied.

s0355.literal: [15] "Fayun Temple monk Huixiu"—the Hall edition's textual verification says "xiu" in the Southern History reads "ba."
s0355.idiomatic: On "[15] Fayun Temple monk Huixiu": the Hall edition notes xiu in the Southern History reads ba.

s0356.literal: [16] "Gu Yue styled Sinan"—the Hall edition's textual verification says "si" in the Southern History reads "yun."
s0356.idiomatic: On "[16] Gu Yue styled Sinan": the Hall edition notes si in the Southern History reads yun.

s0357.literal: [17] "beside connecting variant meanings"—the character "yi" (variant) was an ink dot in the base text; supplied according to all editions.
s0357.idiomatic: On "[17] beside connecting variant meanings": the character yi (variant) was an ink dot in the base text; supplied per all editions.

s0358.literal: [18] "appointed staff counsel to the Prince of Shixing"—the Southern History reads "appointed staff counsel to the Prince of Poyang's Eastern Center Commandant household."
s0358.idiomatic: On "[18] appointed staff counsel to the prince of Shixing": the Southern History reads appointed staff counsel to the prince of Poyang's eastern center commandant household.

s0359.literal: Zhang Senkai's collation note says: "According to the Prince of Poyang Boshan's biography, Boshan once was Eastern Center Commandant—'Prince of Shixing' should follow the Southern History as 'Prince of Poyang.'"
s0359.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai's collation note says: per Prince Poyang Boshan's biography, Boshan once was eastern center commandant—"prince of Shixing" should follow the Southern History as "prince of Poyang."

s0360.literal: [19] "at the time age seventy-eight"—"seventy-eight" in the Southern History reads "seventy-seven."
s0360.idiomatic: On "[19] at the time age seventy-eight": seventy-eight in the Southern History reads seventy-seven.

s0361.literal: [20] "grandfather Dao Bao"—the Hall edition's textual verification says "bao" in the Southern History reads "shi."
s0361.idiomatic: On "[20] grandfather Dao Bao": the Hall edition notes bao in the Southern History reads shi.

s0362.literal: [21] "marriage alliance does not lose kin"—the phrase in the Analects is "yin does not lose kin"; here yin is read as marriage alliance, so "yin" was changed to "marriage yin."
s0362.idiomatic: On "[21] marriage alliance does not lose kin": the Analects reads "yin does not lose kin"; here yin is taken as marriage alliance, so yin was written as marriage yin.

s0363.literal: See Qian Daxin's Collation of the Twenty-Four Histories in detail.
s0363.idiomatic: See Qian Daxin's Collation of the Twenty-Four Histories in detail.

s0364.literal: [22] "hurriedly drew his mother, younger sister, and orphaned nephew into the boat"—the Hall edition's textual verification says "orphan" in the Southern History reads "paternal aunt."
s0364.idiomatic: On "[22] hurriedly drew his mother, younger sister, and orphaned nephew into the boat": the Hall edition notes orphan in the Southern History reads paternal aunt.

s0365.literal: [23] "Yuangui authored Spring and Autumn Opening Topics and Expository Records eleven scrolls"—note: the Jingdian shiwen xulu says Shen Wena authored Spring and Autumn Expository Outline unfinished, and Wang Yuangui continued and completed it.
s0365.idiomatic: On "[23] Yuangui authored Spring and Autumn opening topics and expository records eleven scrolls": the Jingdian shiwen xulu says Shen Wena's Spring and Autumn expository outline was unfinished and Wang Yuangui completed it.

s0366.literal: The Sui Treatise on Bibliography has Wang Yuangui's Continuation of Shen Wena's Zuo Commentary Expository Outline in ten scrolls.
s0366.idiomatic: The Sui Treatise on Bibliography lists Wang Yuangui's continuation of Shen Wena's Zuo Commentary expository outline in ten scrolls.

s0367.literal: This "Expository Records" should be the error for "Expository Outline."
s0367.idiomatic: Expository Records here should be the error for Expository Outline.
